title: Personal Checking: Refund Amount for an Erroneous Overdraft Protection Transfer Fee
content:
## Combination rule

For the most recently posted overdraft protection transfer fee on a Personal Checking account, a single ground of error is sufficient: whenever any ground shows the fee was charged in error, it is a bank error, and grounds never need to coincide.

A fee that is a bank error and has not yet been refunded is refunded **in full**, at exactly the amount the fee entry shows, never a part of it, and the refund is recorded with bank error as its reason. Once a refund entry stands against the fee, no second refund follows, whichever ground might apply. In every other case this policy refunds nothing; if the customer asks for a goodwill refund instead, that request is decided under the courtesy conditions of the general Personal Checking fee refund rules.

Because fee amounts are kept to two decimal places, the refund needs no rounding.

## Truth table

| Charged in error on some ground | Refund entry already exists | Refund under this policy |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | the whole fee amount |
| yes | yes | nothing |
| no | no | nothing |
| no | yes | nothing |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A transfer fee of 14.00 USD is found to be an error and carries no refund: the refund is 14.00 USD, booked as a bank-error correction. If the same fee had been refunded last month, nothing further is refunded.
